headline: GOLD FALLS TO 2026 ANNUAL LOW — $3,852 PRINT THURSDAY, $3,879 WEEKLY CLOSE; FOMC MINUTES AND RETAIL SALES THE RECOVERY TESTS THIS WEEK
snippet: Gold closed Friday November 14 at $3,879 — a weekly loss that leaves it printing its 2026 annual low of $3,852 set Thursday, nearly 15% off the January record. The twin drivers: a 10-year Treasury yield at 5.15% and the US dollar at a 19-month high, with CME FedWatch pricing an 85% implied probability of a December rate hike following Governor Bowman's November 11 inflation comments. Finance Feeds frames the week ahead around two catalysts: US retail sales (Tuesday), which will test whether October's hot CPI was accompanied by genuine consumer demand or a Fed tightening into weakness — the second being historically bullish for gold — and FOMC minutes (Wednesday), where even a split vote on December would pull the implied hike probability back toward 65% and give the relief rally metals bulls need. Bull case for the week: $4,000 recapture; bear case: a weekly close below $3,800, which breaks the 8-month ascending support structure.

headline: SILVER HITS 1-YEAR LOW AT $48.65 — FALLS 2.6% FRIDAY AS FED SIGNALS DECEMBER HIKE, 17% BELOW OCTOBER'S $60 HIGH
snippet: COMEX silver futures fell 2.6% on Friday November 13 to $48.65 — a 12-month low — as Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman's November 11 speech broadened market expectations for persistent inflation and reignited December rate-hike pricing. Silver's move from $60.32 on October 13 to $48.65 is a 17.4% draw-down in 30 days, outpacing gold's roughly 8% correction from its own October peak. The decline is financial-market driven: the Silver Institute projects a 46.3 million ounce structural supply deficit in 2026, the sixth consecutive year of undersupply, with photovoltaic panel manufacturers absorbing approximately 232 million ounces annually — a demand stream not revising orders downward in response to the correction. For retail investors monitoring the silver equity space, the gap between $48.65 spot and the Silver Institute's physical deficit model is as wide as it has been in this bull cycle, which historically precedes a sharp snap-back when the rate narrative shifts.

headline: TUDOR GOLD DRILLS 9.00 g/t OVER 9.5m AT PERFECTSTORM PORPHYRY — HIGH-GRADE PSP ZONE EXTENDS DOWN-DIP AND ALONG STRIKE AT TREATY CREEK
snippet: Tudor Gold (TSXV: TUD) reported the latest results from the Treaty Creek property's Perfectstorm Porphyry (PSP) Zone in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, with the best intersection returning 9.00 g/t gold over 9.50 metres, including 43.29 g/t over 1.20 metres. The PSP Zone is a copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry system; the new holes confirm the zone extends both down-dip and along strike and remains open — meaning the system has not yet been closed off at depth or laterally. For retail investors following Golden Triangle exploration, the PSP Zone is distinct from Treaty Creek's larger Goldstorm system: Goldstorm is the multi-million-ounce bulk-tonnage target, while PSP is the high-grade core that could anchor a higher-margin underground scenario. High-grade intervals like 9.00 g/t over 9.5m in a porphyry setting are unusual — most porphyries average 0.3–0.6 g/t — and the geological argument for Perfectstorm is that it represents the apical core of the porphyry, the highest-grade part of the system.

headline: PROSPECTOR METALS DRILLS 22m AT 5.91 g/t GOLD IN YUKON PHASE 2 — TESS ZONE FOOTPRINT EXPANDS AT FULLY-FUNDED ML PROJECT
snippet: Prospector Metals (TSXV: PPP) released Phase 2 drill results from its ML gold-copper project in the Yukon, with a 22-metre intersection grading 5.91 g/t gold from the TESS Zone. The TESS Zone was opened by discovery hole ML25-031, which returned 44 metres at 13.79 g/t gold and 1.84% copper in 2025; the new Phase 2 work tests whether that discovery hole represents a narrow high-grade vein or the edge of a larger system. With the zone now defined over a 200-metre trend and 150-metre depth, Phase 2 results suggest the latter. Prospector's 25,000-metre 2026 program is fully funded — an important distinction in a market where exploration companies are cutting programs. For retail investors, the combination of a funded multi-hole program, a 44m @ 13.79 g/t discovery hole as the geological anchor, and consistent Phase 2 follow-up at the TESS Zone puts Prospector in the category of junior explorers with enough geological evidence to support a thesis, not just a first-hole press release.

headline: 30-DAY COMMODITY SCORECARD: LITHIUM LEADS SELLOFF AT -14.7% — URANIUM AT $91.85/LB IS THE LONE STANDOUT AT +18% YEAR-OVER-YEAR
snippet: A 30-day commodity performance snapshot through November 13 shows lithium carbonate down 14.7% — the worst performer — driven by soft EV demand and ample Chinese domestic supply. Copper is off 7%, silver 17%, and gold 8% over the same period. The single standout is uranium at $91.85 per pound, up 18.14% year-over-year and positive on a 30-day basis while virtually every other commodity in the complex is in the red. Nickel at +3.7% is the only other commodity in positive territory. For retail investors managing commodity sector exposure, the data makes the divergence between uranium and the rest of the electrification metals complex unusually stark: lithium and copper are the correction story this month, while uranium is running on a structurally different thesis — nuclear plant life extensions, AI data centre power demand, and utility contracting cycles that are largely decoupled from EV market sentiment.

headline: GOLD BEARS HOLD BELOW $4,150 — ROBOFOREX TARGETS $3,778 FLOOR IN 16-20 NOVEMBER WINDOW AS DOLLAR AND YIELDS DOMINATE
snippet: RoboForex's weekly gold technical analysis published November 13 sets the bearish control line at $4,150: while price remains below that resistance, the bias is to sell rallies rather than buy dips. The near-term support structure is $3,852 — last week's low and the 2026 annual low — with a measured move target of $3,778 as the base of an 8-month ascending pattern that would be violated on a weekly close below $3,800. The fundamental backdrop reinforcing the technical bear case is the 5.15% 10-year Treasury yield (the highest since the 2007 credit crisis) and a dollar at a 19-month peak, both of which suppress gold's opportunity cost argument. For retail investors using technical analysis to time entries, the $3,778–$3,852 zone represents the technical support cluster where risk-reward for initiating or adding to gold positions is most favourable in this correction — but only if retail sales and FOMC minutes this week don't surprise to the hawkish side, which would invalidate that support range.
